title: t064 — Toonsi-vs-Han2024 directed-axis agreement (hypothesis:0002-directed-disease-relations-axis circularity-tell, the load-bearing check)
paragraph:
**Confirmatory substrate (denominator, locked).** The **direct ICD-10 3-char route** (lock 2), *not* the
MeSH crosswalk. Both sources are ICD-10 family (Toonsi ICD-10-CM, Han ICD-10), so the MeSH detour is an
unnecessary, lossy bottleneck — ⟢ it covered only 34 shared nodes / 561 dyads vs. **138 shared nodes /
18,906 ordered pairs** direct. The shared node universe is ⟢ **138 ICD-10 3-char codes**
(Toonsi 752 ∩ Han 190; 72.6% of Han's space). Ordered-pair universe = ⟢ **18,906** (138×137); the
primary outcome is **directed** (ordered), so the unit is the ordered pair, not the unordered dyad.
**Granularity sensitivity (single locked operation): exclude** Toonsi 3-char nodes with fan-in ≥ 3 ⚠
(⟢ 255/752 nodes; median fan-in = 2, so ≥ 3 is above-typical) and re-run the primary verdict on the
reduced node set. "Exclude" is the locked operation — degree-weighted down-weighting is **exploratory
only** (it changes the statistic, not just the universe, and is not verdict-bearing).

title: t064 confirmatory directed-concordance QAP supports "Toonsi agrees with Han2024
paragraph:
The pre-registered confirmatory directed-concordance QAP (`pre-registration:0014`, all G1–G4 gates
green) measured, on the shared ICD-10 3-char universe (138 nodes / 18,906 ordered pairs; 610 Toonsi /
220 Han-sig directed edges), an observed concordance of **56 vs a degree-preserving node-label QAP
null mean of 7.05 → enrichment 7.94×, permutation p < 1e-4** (observed exceeds all 10,000 degree-
preserving relabelings), phi 0.137. The agreement strengthens under every stricter Han-positive
definition (FDR 8.47× / magnitude 10.45× / both-sex 15.41×, each p < 1e-4), survives the fan-in
granularity sensitivity (73 nodes, 8.20×), the E_floor sweep {1.5,2.0,3.0}, and is direction-specific
(43 concordant vs 16 anti, p = 3e-4). This directly establishes
`proposition:t064-toonsi-agrees-with-han-progression`.

paragraph:

title: Per-disease neighbour/contributor delta inspection for alt-view newly-elevated
paragraph: The t031 hypothesis — that the six alt-view "newly elevated" diseases jump in cross-axis-divergence rank *because publication-gravity removal swaps canon contributors for disease-specific contributors and reshuffles the gene-axis nearest-neighbour structure* — is now mechanistically confirmed for every one of the six diseases. The raw → alt switch (a) drops the canon share of top-50 gene-contributors from 30–42% to **0%**, (b) shifts the d_g median of top-50 contributors from ~3800 (near the maximum) into the configured 1000–3000 window, and (c) reorders the gene-axis nearest neighbours from biologically unrelated diseases under raw to **textbook biology** under alt (lysosomal storage diseases for MPS-IV, organic acidurias for isovaleric acidemia, bone-marrow-failure syndromes for Shwachman-Diamond, GI motility disorders for Megacolon, primate / zoonotic diseases for Monkey Diseases, dental/dermal reactions for Gingival Hyperplasia).

title: t079 GWAS-rg axis coverage scout — does genetic-correlation clear §c.0, and if not where is it the right tool?
paragraph:
**Ceiling 1 — phenotype count vs cluster size.** Sakaue's **159 total phenotypes** is
already **below** the 60% gate for clusters 2 (424) and 7 (249): even if *every* Sakaue
phenotype mapped into a single cluster, it could not cover 60% of those two HC clusters.
For clusters 6 (184) and 8 (179) it is arithmetically *possible* only if ~115% / ~113% of

every gate.

title: t016 crosswalk probe \u2014 UMLS-anchored MeSH\u2192ICD-10 on the t054/Dong\
paragraph:

`{t046, t047, t054}`, the **only** consumer is **t054 Dong** — t046/t047 are
MeSH-native (closed-label-space, no crosswalk), and t053/t055 are deferred to
v2. So the entire near-term value of t016 is one mapping direction:
**MeSH → ICD-10 level-2**, the disease-id space of Dong2021's 439 common
diseases.

title: Synthesis: h01-molecular-truth-axis
paragraph: The structural backbone is solid. Cross-axis ARI(genes, symptoms) = 0.190 raw / 0.220 alt-view under a row-wise permutation null (z = 221 raw, z = 598 alt, p = 0/100 in both views), established by task t007 and documented in `entities/interpretations/0001-cross-axis-taxonomy-divergence.md`. This divergence survives all nine publication-gravity-suppressed normalizations tested (ARI range 0.218–0.278), placing the structural claim on solid footing per tasks t027/t028/t029. Under a principled PPMI-SVD correction (task t076), the ARI lands at 0.233 inside the pre-registered corrected band and is k-stable; however the clip is load-bearing (signed PMI without clipping reverts to 0.189), qualifying the result as suggestive per `entities/interpretations/0012-ppmi-svd-axis-disease-track.md`.

paragraph:

title: Do diseases that share pleiotropic rCNV segments from [@Collins2022] co-cluster
paragraph: Collins et al. 2022 identified 178 disease-associated rCNV segments across 54 HPO-mapped disease phenotypes, including a set of "pleiotropic" segments associated with multiple phenotypes. These pleiotropic segments are more gene-dense and overlap more mutationally constrained genes than monoassociated segments, suggesting they represent genuinely shared genomic vulnerability loci. The question is whether the pair of diseases that share a pleiotropic rCNV segment also co-cluster under the PubTator gene axis — a finding that would be consistent with `hypothesis:0001-molecular-truth-axis`'s claim that the gene axis captures shared molecular biology. Disagreement (rCNV-pleiotropic diseases *not* co-clustering in the gene axis) would suggest that the gene axis misses structurally shared genetic architecture.

title: t077 discriminating regression — inconclusive-for-coverage (GWAS-rg leg fails G2)
paragraph:
Admissible cohort coverage (diseases mapping 1:1 to a source's GWAS phenotypes through the
high-confidence MeSH↔ICD10 crosswalk, dropping both fan-out and fan-in collapses — pre-reg cohort
rule 4), against the eligible {2,6,7,8} cohort (1,623 diseases, broad labels excluded per rule 2):

title: Gene-axis CVD similarity should reproduce the GWAS-rg AF/CAD/VTE vs HF/PAD/Stroke
paragraph:
If the PubTator gene axis tracks molecular truth (`hypothesis:0001-molecular-truth-axis`), then
gene-axis similarity among the project's cardiovascular-disease entities should reproduce the
**genetic subgroup structure** that GWAS genetic correlations reveal: `cite:Qiao2025Cardio` finds all
15/15 pairwise rg > 0 (median 0.435) across six CVDs but with a clear cleavage between an
**AF/CAD/VTE** cluster and an **HF/PAD/Stroke** cluster. Concretely: the gene-axis CVD
sub-matrix, clustered, should place AF, CAD, and VTE closer to one another than to HF, PAD, and
Stroke (and vice versa), recovering the same split. This is a **falsifiable, non-circular test** —
the rg matrix is derived from public GWAS summary statistics, not from literature co-mention, so
agreement is evidence the gene axis carries molecular structure rather than publication framing.

title: t077 discriminating regression — inconclusive-for-coverage (GWAS-rg leg fails G2)
paragraph:
A perfect GWAS source covering every crosswalkable disease would still cap at the **crosswalk
ceiling**: 378 cohort diseases carry an exact ICD10 mapping (888 under exact+narrower+broader) — far
above 50. The binding constraint is that the biobank atlases have simply **not run GWAS** on most of
this cohort's complex diseases; only ~34 of them are GWAS'd in the broadest single source.

title: Critical review \u2014 v1 pre-registration stack (t041 v1.3 + t017 v1.0 +\
paragraph: Clause 5 says "Demela cells would have `mapping_coverage ≈ 0.085` against typical PubTator clusters." The 0.085 figure corresponds to `|members_C| / |cluster_size|` for `|members_C| = 4` (max-likely Demela members in any one cluster) against a cluster of size ~47. But t054 v1.1's expected outcomes (lines 80–86) report PubTator k=10 cluster sizes are 154–721 (mean 383) — so realistic Demela mapping_coverage is 4/154 ≈ 0.026 to 4/721 ≈ 0.006. The "0.085" figure may originate from an older PubTator cluster snapshot or a different cluster-membership rule.

title: t047 \u2014 Lim2025 proteostasis 3-state taxonomy vs PubTator gene-axis (32-disease\
paragraph: **Note that k=4 in t047 is one boundary higher than k=4 in t046.** Under t046's (3, 4, 2) marginal, min_p(4) = 1/126 ≈ 0.008 ≤ 0.05 (confirmatory). Under t047's (12, 5, 15) marginal, min_p(4) = 0.0519 > 0.05 (NOT confirmatory). The asymmetry comes from the marginal: t046's (3, 4, 2) total = 9 has much higher prior probability of an all-one-factor sample at k=4 (1/126 = max-state's a priori share at C(9,4)) than t047's (12, 5, 15) total = 32 (purity-1 requires picking 4 of 32 all from the same state, much rarer). Combinatorially derived, defensible.

title: t017 \u2014 Axis selection and aggregation (v1 family BH-FDR + verdict close)
paragraph: "The aggregator's §c.0 assessability gate branches by `null_design_family`: closed-label-space cells are assessable iff `stage2_pass AND confirmatory_eligible` (probe-side combinatorial gate is operative); broad-marginal-matched cells additionally require `mapping_coverage ≥ 0.60` (aggregator-side coverage gate is operative). `mapping_coverage` is REQUIRED as a canonical-schema column for every cell in both families (transparency); only its enforcement at the §c.0 gate is family-conditional. The rationale: closed-label-space axes have a fundamentally different under-identification mechanic — `|members_C|` against a small bounded axis-label set — than broad-marginal axes have. The two families' gates measure different things; gating them with the same threshold is structurally inappropriate (Demela cells would have `mapping_coverage` in the range ~0.005–0.030 against current PubTator k=10 clusters of size 154–721 — sub-percent magnitudes, well below the 0.60 rule, regardless of how concentrated Demela is in any one cluster). This clause refines t041 v1.2 §c.0 at the per-probe level per t041's §Amendment Procedure (per-probe pre-regs can pin per-probe interpretations of framework rul

title: Sharpen disease operational definition and add symptom axis
paragraph:
Currently the `disease-similarity` pipeline treats every MeSH term tagged by PubTator as
"disease" entity type as a disease. PubTator's tagging is broad: of the 10,662 entities
in the disease label set for PubTator 2026-03-17, ~5,121 are MeSH descriptors,
~4,756 are MeSH supplementary concepts (SCRs), 785 are OMIM identifiers, and the
descriptor set itself includes many things that are not diseases proper —
classical signs and symptoms (Pain, Fatigue, Fever), anatomical pathological
conditions, wounds and injuries.

title: t017 \u2014 Axis selection and aggregation (v1 family BH-FDR + verdict close)
paragraph: "Empirical p-values from probes using exact enumeration (closed-label-space family) and probes using Monte Carlo sampling (broad-marginal-matched family) are pooled in a single global BH-FDR family at q ≤ 0.05 per t041 §c.2.1. The validity of this pooling rests on each axis individually passing its Stage-2 diagnostic (ii) p-value uniformity check on its own data. The aggregator does not re-correct for the differing resolution floors of the two null constructions; a sensitivity layer (WP6) reports the band-shift under collapsed Monte Carlo resolution floors as an audit of pooling robustness."

title: Synthesis: h01-molecular-truth-axis
paragraph: The per-disease Track A P1 test failed: F1 triggered 6/6 for complex diseases (Jaccard < 0.05, p > 0.05), attributed to the publication-gravity/popularity-vs-effect-size mechanism (`entities/interpretations/0008-h01-phase1-results.md`). Bias-suppressed re-run (task t067) rescued only 2/6; Glioblastoma was a robust non-rescue at ample windowed coverage (`entities/interpretations/0007-h01-p1-altview-sensitivity.md`). The single Track B case — Long QT Syndrome — is the hypothesis's cleanest positive: recall@100 of a curated ion-channel panel doubles from 0.389 (raw, inconclusive zone) to 0.778 (alt-view and PPMI, pass range), with cluster-mate AUC of 0.967 (raw) / 0.928 (PPMI-SVD), well above both the symptom axis (0.810) and matched null. This positive rests on n = 1 and is framed by question:0014-monogenic-vs-polygenic-gene-axis-scope as the key open question.

title: EHR trajectories and patient embeddings \u2014 cross-paper synthesis
paragraph: **D2 — How much does ordering add beyond co-occurrence?** `id:Edelman2025`'s reverse-order RR 1.21 and `id:Beaney2024`'s modest sequence-model gains suggest ordering matters but is not dominant. `id:Placido2024`'s review is more optimistic, citing 80% of cancer events predicted ahead of time from trajectories. The difference is partly endpoint-specific (acute cancer onset vs general 1-year outcomes) and partly evaluation-frame (event-time prediction vs binary AUC). For `hypothesis:0002-directed-disease-relations-axis` the conservative read is that directionality buys 10–25% over symmetric co-occurrence, not an order of magnitude.

title: h03 cross-axis falsification thresholds
paragraph: Define the **assessable subset**: high-confidence clusters (§c.1) that also clear the §c.0 assessability rule (≥3 axes in ≥2 categories with ≥60% mapping coverage AND on axes that passed the §Pilot Calibration Stage 2 null-diagnostic).

paragraph: The offset bands (100 / 200 / 300 / 400 / 500 / 1000+) are spaced widely enough that no two MC operations can collide on a single integer seed across any feasible k-grid or cluster set (k-grid is small, ≤ 10 entries; PubTator clusters are 1..10).

title: Publication gravity as a confounder of literature-derived gene similarity
paragraph: The raw and alt views were cross-referenced in `doc/probes/2026-05-17-alt-view-ranking-validation/`. Headline: **zero overlap in the top 25**, only 2 entries shared in top 50 (Pars Planitis, Amyloidosis), 21 shared in top 100. Rank Spearman across the full overlap is 0.456; value Pearson on `mean_disagreement` is 0.691 — modest correlation, but the *head* of the ranking is qualitatively disjoint. Six alt-top-50 entries are *newly elevated* (raw `mean_disagreement < 0.7` → alt > 0.8): Mucopolysaccharidosis IV, Acidemia isovaleric, Shwachman-Diamond, Gingival Hyperplasia, Megacolon, Monkey Diseases. Their raw `disagreement_genes_vs_symptoms` is ~0.57–0.59 — raw was not declaring them undivergent, just ranking them well outside the head. Attributing the rank jump *causally* to publication-gravity removal requires a per-disease neighbour/contributor delta inspection that this probe does not perform. The two views are best cited as separate working lists; the top-100 intersection (21 diseases) is a **normalization-robust candidate core** (robust only across raw and `log1p_idf_dg_window` at fixed k, filters, corpus, and ranking-metric definition — not yet k- or corpus-robust).

title: Alt-view ranking validation: bidirectional raw-vs-alt comparison + low-data
paragraph: These are diseases the raw view ranked low / less divergent; the alt view sharply increases their gene-vs-symptom disagreement. The raw `disagreement_genes_vs_symptoms` for these six is ~0.57–0.59 (not zero — raw was not declaring them undivergent, just well outside the head of the ranking). The two views *qualitatively disagree on whether to surface them*. Proving that publication gravity itself is the *causal mechanism* (rather than e.g. d_g-window-specific neighbour reshuffling) requires a per-disease neighbour / contributor delta inspection — flagged below as the natural t031 follow-up.

title: Undirected PubTator co-occurrence substantially predicts Toonsi directed-edge
paragraph:
On the clean 1:1 MeSH substrate (190 covered diseases; 394 unordered directed-relation dyads
over a C(190,2)=17,955 candidate universe; base rate 2.19%), undirected PubTator co-occurrence
similarity ranks true Toonsi directed pairs above non-pairs at **joint AUROC 0.728** (co-occurrence
+ gene axes; censored node-label-permutation **p < 1e-4** — the observed statistic exceeds all
10,000 degree-preserving relabelings). Co-occurrence carries essentially all of it (per-axis AUROC
0.728); the gene axis predicts moderately alone (0.655) but its joint coefficient collapses to ~0.02
under collinearity (Spearman 0.62). The predictability **survives publication-gravity adjustment**:
gravity-only AUROC 0.639, with the undirected axes adding a significant +0.105 increment (p < 1e-3).

title: Project synthesis - pan-disease
paragraph: **`hypothesis:0007-care-process-ascertainment-artifact` — care-process / ascertainment artifact (candidate).** The clinical analogue of `hypothesis:0006-research-program-co-study-structure`: a share of disease-disease relatedness reflects how patients are surveilled, coded, and co-diagnosed (shared specialties, screening cascades, healthcare-utilization intensity) rather than biology. It bears most on the co-occurrence and *directed* axes — for `hypothesis:0002-directed-disease-relations-axis` it is the dominant alternative to causal progression (clinical coding records complications after diagnosis). Operationalized via a proxy ladder (specialty → procedure/screening → utilization intensity → EHR co-management) with a pre-registered "material fraction" threshold (≥20% variance/edge absorption). Downstream of the same crosswalk as `hypothesis:0003-multi-axis-validation`/`hypothesis:0002-directed-disease-relations-axis`.

title: Literature-mined disease-gene associations \u2014 cross-paper synthesis
paragraph: **5. Scale-free hub structure recurs across operationalizations.** Zhang's per-topic disease-gene networks are uniformly power-law (231–608 nodes, 799–10,895 edges, diameter 5–8 across 10 focal topics), and the LVD locus analysis in Deo finds that 10 of 11 multi-genic loci have a known cardiomyopathy gene as top-ranked (odds ratio 7.65, P = 8×10^-5) — both consistent with the project's recurring observation that a small number of universal "textbook" genes (EGFR, TP53, APOE, etc.) dominate gene_cor inflation across well-studied disease pairs. The hub structure is mechanically what publication gravity looks like at network level.

title: Gene-axis disease similarity reflects shared molecular biology, not just shared literature framing
paragraph: > **Amendment (2026-05-23, `plan:0016-`hypothesis:0001-molecular-truth-axis`-p2p3-descriptive-redesign-design`).** A pre-real-run code review found the F2/F3 verdict path (per-member decile+subtree-matched null + permutation GSEA) infeasible at real cluster scale (gene-axis cluster sizes 154–721 vs matched candidate pools of 10–29; ~18k prerank calls). Per the 2026-05-23 disposition, **P2/P3 is demoted from a falsification test to a descriptive cross-axis effect size** (Mann-Whitney AUC of the focal disease's molecular reference in the gene-axis vs symptom-axis cluster-mate profiles, plus a feasible distribution-matched random baseline). Consequently **F2 and F3 are no longer adjudicated by phase 1.** Only **F1 / P1** (Track A DEG recovery, Track B panel recall) remains a phase-1 falsification criterion. The phase-1 interpretation note (B.5.2) MUST NOT claim `hypothesis:0001-molecular-truth-axis` support or refutation from the P2/P3 descriptive output; every P2/P3 output row is stamped `analysis_mode = "descriptive"` to guard against this. The F2/F3 definitions above are retained as the design reference for a future confirmatory pass (a publication-gravity-controlled null at real c

title: Next Steps \u2014 2026-05-31
paragraph:
All three hypotheses remain **`proposed`**; all questions **`active`**. None formally reviewed
in 365 days despite a frozen v1 verdict (`hypothesis:0003-multi-axis-validation`) and a real phase-1 result (`hypothesis:0001-molecular-truth-axis`).

title: Tissue/organ confound: GTEx-reference residualization (q0016) and within-vs-cross-organ agreement decomposition (q0018)
paragraph:
The data-internal **PC-removal** control (`interpretation:0010`) drove LUAD–BLCA
**+0.605 → −0.346 (PC1) → −0.551 (PC1+2)** but **reshuffled** the whole structure
(near-flat spectrum 0.299/0.177/0.176/0.152/0.132/0.064, n_diseases≈n_components):
after PC1 the carcinomas spuriously grouped *with* GBM (BLCA–GBM +0.529, LUAD–GBM
+0.400) and after PC1+2 a spurious DCM–MM +0.703 appeared.
